description:
Today `transport/libp2p.New` constructs and owns its `host.Host`. Callers that already run a libp2p host — or that want to run additional libp2p protocols (gossipsub, application-specific RPCs) on the *same* identity — have no way to share it.

Shepherd is the motivating consumer: a shepherd-d daemon wants exactly one libp2p identity per host. If shepherd keeps its own host and mosey opens a second one alongside, the daemon presents two peer IDs, opens two sets of listening ports, and can't share an established connection between, say, a forwarder RPC and a `/mosey/pty/` attach.

Two shapes that solve it:

1. **`Config.Host host.Host`** — if non-nil, the backend uses the supplied host and skips constructing one. `Close` does not shut the host down (caller owns it).
2. **`(*Backend).Host() host.Host` accessor** — backend still owns construction, but external code can register additional protocols / open pubsub on the same host.

(1) is more flexible and lets shepherd own bring-up + identity / addr config. (2) is less invasive but pushes ownership inversion onto the consumer.

Workaround path if this never lands: shepherd keeps mosey strictly behind `transport.Transport` and runs its own forwarder protocol as a mosey-registered `Handle`. That covers the forwarder case but not gossipsub or any other libp2p-direct feature, so this remains a real-but-bounded ceiling on what consumers can do.

Depends on `ship-y2s` (public Go API surface) — without that, no external caller can hit this code path.
title: BYO libp2p host (or expose the host) on the libp2p backend
